From Mctt.Core.Syntactic.Levels Require Export Ordinals.

An item of an open: (Some n, d, pv) declares d as the member n of the opened module, (None, d, pv) declares d as the opened module itself; private when pv. The surface syntax and the core share it.
Definition iitem : Set := (option string * string * bool)%type.

Concrete Syntax Tree

Module Cst.

Modifiers

private hides a definition from importers, abstract makes its body opaque. The two are orthogonal, hence a record rather than a variant.
Record mods : Set :=
  { md_private : bool
  ; md_abstract : bool }.

Definition md_pub : mods := {| md_private := false; md_abstract := false |}.
Definition md_priv : mods := {| md_private := true; md_abstract := false |}.
Definition md_abs : mods := {| md_private := false; md_abstract := true |}.
Definition md_priv_abs : mods := {| md_private := true; md_abstract := true |}.

Definition Keywords

def and its shorthands. Each keyword implies some modifiers, and takes the others: theorem and lemma are abstract def and take private; fact and remark are abstract private def and take none; let and given are private def and take abstract. A modifier the keyword already implies is rejected.
Inductive definition_keyword : Set :=
| definition_keyword_def | definition_keyword_theorem | definition_keyword_lemma | definition_keyword_fact | definition_keyword_remark | definition_keyword_let | definition_keyword_given.

Definition definition_keyword_name (k : definition_keyword) : string :=
  match k with
  | definition_keyword_def => "def" | definition_keyword_theorem => "theorem" | definition_keyword_lemma => "lemma"
  | definition_keyword_fact => "fact" | definition_keyword_remark => "remark" | definition_keyword_let => "let" | definition_keyword_given => "given"
  end.

The modifiers of m k, or why k rejects m.
Definition definition_keyword_mods (k : definition_keyword) (m : mods) : (mods + string)%type :=
  match k with
  | definition_keyword_def => inl m
  | definition_keyword_theorem | definition_keyword_lemma =>
      if md_abstract m then inr (definition_keyword_name k ++ " is already abstract")%string
      else inl {| md_private := md_private m; md_abstract := true |}
  | definition_keyword_fact | definition_keyword_remark =>
      if orb (md_private m) (md_abstract m) then inr (definition_keyword_name k ++ " takes no modifiers")%string
      else inl md_priv_abs
  | definition_keyword_let | definition_keyword_given =>
      if md_private m then inr (definition_keyword_name k ++ " is already private")%string
      else inl {| md_private := true; md_abstract := md_abstract m |}
  end.

Objects, Declarations and Commands

The two levels of naming are spelled differently. :: separates the segments of a file path, the name of a compilation unit, which is what glob holds; . selects a member of whatever precedes it, be that an internal module, a unit, or a local module.
proj is that postfix dot: X::Y::Z.W.foo is a chain of projs over glob ["X"; "Y"; "Z"], and A.foo for a module A is one over var "A". Module arguments arrive as ordinary app nodes, so (X::Y.Z a b).foo needs no syntax of its own. Whether a var, a proj or an app is a module or a term is decided by its position: the head of a proj, the head of an application in such a head, an alias body and an open target are modules, everything else is a term.
letb binds one declaration at a time; the parser folds the bindings of let x : A := a; y : B := b in body end into nested letbs.
A module declaration has one shape at the top level and in a let: its parameters, and its definition mdef, a body where cmds end or an alias := E. The body of a local module is the same list of commands as that of a global one. The branches of an eliminator, the parameters and the fields are nested through lists of pairs, all of which have All schemes registered (Core.Base): the mutual principle cst_ind below is generated.
Inductive expression : Set :=
Typeω@i, a large universe, the universe ω²+i, written Type@{ω^2} for i = 0 and Type@{ω^2+i}; ω^2 is not a level.
| typ : nat -> expression
Type@{M}, the small universe at the level M
| suniv : expression -> expression
Level@n, the type of the levels below ω·(n+1); Level is Level@0
| level : nat -> expression
A level literal ω·a + b, written <b>l when a is 0 and also <b>L when a is 1
| llit : o2 -> expression
succl M
| succl : expression -> expression
maxl M N
| maxl : expression -> expression -> expression
Nat or ℕ: the type bound by builtin natural
| nat : expression
A numeral, of the type bound by builtin natural
| num : nat -> expression
True
| true_ty : expression
true
| true_tm : expression
False
| false_ty : expression
exfalso M return x . A
| exfalso : expression -> string -> expression -> expression
forall (x : A) -> B
| pi : string -> expression -> expression -> expression
fun (x : A) -> M
| fn : string -> expression -> expression -> expression
M N: a function or a module applied
| app : expression -> expression -> expression
A name: a local variable, a module, or a member in scope
| var : string -> expression
A :: path, hence at least two segments after a var; a unit of one segment is written as a var
| glob : list string -> expression
M.x: a member of a module
| proj : expression -> string -> expression
let d in M end, one declaration at a time
| letb : decl -> expression -> expression
elim M at xs (z : Z) -> A | c ys ⇒ B … with … end: the eliminator of a group of inductive types, one block per member in member order, the one marked at (true) the scrutinee's. A block's binders, the non-uniform parameters then the scrutinee, outermost first, each with its type if written; its motive under them; its branches, each binding the non-uniform parameters, the constructor's arguments and the induction hypotheses, in that order
| elim : expression -> list (bool * list (string * option expression) * expression * list (string * list string * expression)) -> expression
record T where f := M ; … end: a value of the record type T, its fields in order, each its name and its value
| tuple : expression -> list (string * expression) -> expression

with decl : Set :=
x : A := M, or x := M without the type. A local definition is always transparent and has no modifiers.
| d_def : string -> option expression -> expression -> decl
module X (ps) md
| d_mod : string -> list (string * expression) -> mdef -> decl

with mdef : Set :=
where cs end
| md_where : list cmd -> mdef
:= E
| md_alias : expression -> mdef

A module declaration carries its name, its parameter telescope and its definition; a unit's own name is declared by prog below, not here. A dotted declaration module A.B is parsed as nested ones (c_mod_dotted).
with cmd : Set :=
private module x (ps) md, private when the flag is set
| c_mod : bool -> string -> list (string * expression) -> mdef -> cmd
private abstract def x : A := M end, with its modifiers
| c_def : mods -> string -> expression -> expression -> cmd
axiom x : A, a definition with no body; it takes no modifiers.
| c_axiom : string -> expression -> cmd
import X::Y loads the unit X::Y, so that it may be named. It declares nothing.
| c_import : list string -> cmd
c_open fq ip args its opens the module at member path ip of the unit fq, applied to args, and declares the items its; an empty fq names the module ip in scope. It loads nothing. So open A.B use (x) is c_open nil ["A"; "B"] nil [(Some "x", "x", true)], and open X::Y Nat export (f as g) is c_open ["X"; "Y"] nil [nat] [(Some "f", "g", false)]. as W is the item (None, "W", true) (open_cmds).
| c_open : list string -> list string -> list expression -> list iitem -> cmd
A command the parser rejects, with the reason, which elaboration reports: a definition keyword with a modifier it already implies (def_cmd).
| c_error : string -> cmd
eval M normalizes M and prints the result; eval M : A additionally checks M against A rather than inferring its type.
| c_eval : expression -> option expression -> cmd
private inductive x (ps) : T where | c (args) … with y : U where … end: the group's uniform parameters ps, shared, and its members, in order: each its name, its type, which binds its non-uniform parameters in front of the sort, forall (n : A) -> S, and its constructors with their arguments. The members' names are in scope in every argument. The second flag says whether the group files its recursor module Rec, as one declared by mutual T where does.
| c_ind : bool -> bool -> list (string * expression) -> list (string * expression * list (string * list (string * expression))) -> cmd
private abstract mutual def (Δ) f (ys) (z : Z) : A := | c xs ⇒ B … with g … end, with its modifiers: the common parameters Δ, and the functions, each its name, its parameters (the non-uniform ones, then the scrutinee, last), its result type and its clauses.
| c_mdef : mods -> list (string * expression) -> list (string * list (string * expression) * expression * list (string * list string * expression)) -> cmd
builtin k := X: binds the inductive type X as the builtin k; natural is the one kind.
| c_builtin : string -> expression -> cmd
private inductive x (ps) := X Ms: an inductive alias, the inductive type X at the arguments Ms, under the parameters ps.
| c_ind_alias : bool -> string -> list (string * expression) -> expression -> cmd
private record x (ps) := X Ms: a record alias, the record type X at the arguments Ms, under the parameters ps.
| c_record_alias : bool -> string -> list (string * expression) -> expression -> cmd
private record x (ps) : S where f : A ; … with cs end: a record type, private when the flag is set: its parameters ps, its sort S, its fields in order, each its name and its type over the fields before it, and its with-area cs, the commands of its module after the fields (none without with).
| c_record : bool -> string -> list (string * expression) -> expression -> list (string * expression) -> list cmd -> cmd.

The mutual induction principle of the family, generated: a list, a pair and an option carry list_all, prod_all and option_all of the motives (Core.Base).
Scheme expression_mut_ind := Induction for expression Sort Prop
with decl_mut_ind := Induction for decl Sort Prop
with mdef_mut_ind := Induction for mdef Sort Prop
with cmd_mut_ind := Induction for cmd Sort Prop.
Combined Scheme cst_ind from expression_mut_ind, decl_mut_ind, mdef_mut_ind, cmd_mut_ind.

module A₁.….Aₙ.B (ps) md is module A₁ where … module Aₙ where module B (ps) md end … end: each Aᵢ has no parameters and the one member Aᵢ₊₁. The grammar gives the path reversed, B first. Only B, the module declared, carries the privacy pv; the Aᵢ are public.
Definition c_mod_dotted (pv : bool) (x : string) (rev_pre : list string) (ps : list (string * expression)) (md : mdef) : cmd :=
  List.fold_left (fun c y => c_mod false y nil (md_where (c :: nil))) rev_pre (c_mod pv x ps md).

k x : A := M end with the modifiers m: the definition, or the rejection of m.
Definition def_cmd (k : definition_keyword) (m : mods) (x : string) (A M : expression) : cmd :=
  match definition_keyword_mods k m with
  | inl m' => c_def m' x A M
  | inr e => c_error e
  end.

mutual k (Δ) f … with g … end with the modifiers m, k a definition keyword: the mutual definition with the modifiers k gives it, as def_cmd gives a single definition, or the rejection of m.
Definition mdef_cmd (k : definition_keyword) (m : mods) (ps : list (string * expression))
    (fs : list (string * list (string * expression) * expression * list (string * list string * expression))) : cmd :=
  match definition_keyword_mods k m with
  | inl m' => c_mdef m' ps fs
  | inr e => c_error e
  end.

axiom x : A with the modifiers m: the axiom, or the rejection of m.
Definition axiom_cmd (m : mods) (x : string) (A : expression) : cmd :=
  if orb (md_private m) (md_abstract m) then c_error "axiom takes no modifiers" else c_axiom x A.

mutual T (ps) where inductive … end end with the modifiers m: the module T, private with m, holding the group and its recursor module T.Rec, or the rejection of abstract.
Definition mutual_cmd (m : mods) (g : string) (ps : list (string * expression))
    (ms : list (string * expression * list (string * list (string * expression)))) : cmd :=
  if md_abstract m then c_error "a group of inductive types takes no abstract"
  else c_mod (md_private m) g nil (md_where (c_ind false true ps ms :: nil)).

open E as W its is open E as W then open W its: the items refer to the alias, and an open declares either the module or its members.
Definition open_cmds (fq ip : list string) (args : list expression) (oW : option string) (its : list iitem)
  : list cmd :=
  match oW with
  | None => c_open fq ip args its :: nil
  | Some W =>
      c_open fq ip args ((None, W, true) :: nil) ::
        match its with
        | nil => nil
        | _ => c_open nil (W :: nil) nil its :: nil
        end
  end.

import X::Y ip args as W its is import X::Y then open X::Y ip args as W its; a bare import X::Y only loads.
Definition import_cmds (fq ip : list string) (args : list expression) (oW : option string) (its : list iitem)
  : list cmd :=
  c_import fq ::
    match ip, args, oW, its with
    | nil, nil, None, nil => nil
    | _, _, _, _ => open_cmds fq ip args oW its
    end.

A leading import or open, before the unit's header, may not export: the commands, or their rejection.
Definition lead_cmds (cs : list cmd) : list cmd :=
  if List.existsb (fun c => match c with
                            | c_open _ _ _ its => List.existsb (fun it => negb (snd it)) its
                            | _ => false
                            end) cs
  then c_error "export is not allowed before the module header" :: nil
  else cs.

A compilation unit: its leading imports and opens, and the one module declaration everything else it contains lives in. That declaration names the unit, so its path is a :: one, and carries the unit's parameters. Only imports and opens may precede it, so no definition is ever made outside a module; the grammar admits nothing else there.
Definition prog : Set := (list cmd * (list string * list (string * expression) * list cmd))%type.

End Cst.

Names and Paths

A unit is named by its path, X::Y::Z, the list "X"; "Y"; "Z"; units do not nest, so a path is flat. The syntax names only units (me_unit); a member of a unit is spelled as a chain of selections from it, me_mem and a_mem.
Abbreviation path := (list string).

Definition path_eq_dec := List.list_eq_dec String.string_dec.

Definition path_beq (fp fq : list string) : bool :=
  if path_eq_dec fp fq then true else false.

Lemma path_beq_refl : forall fp, path_beq fp fp = true.
Proof. intros; unfold path_beq; destruct (path_eq_dec fp fp); congruence. Qed.

Lemma path_beq_true : forall fp fq, path_beq fp fq = true -> fp = fq.
Proof. intros * H; unfold path_beq in H; destruct (path_eq_dec fp fq); congruence. Qed.

Lemma path_beq_false : forall fp fq, fp <> fq -> path_beq fp fq = false.
Proof. intros * H; unfold path_beq; destruct (path_eq_dec fp fq); congruence. Qed.

strip_prefix l m is m with the prefix l removed, if it is one.
Fixpoint strip_prefix (l m : list string) : option (list string) :=
  match l, m with
  | nil, _ => Some m
  | x :: l', y :: m' => if String.eqb x y then strip_prefix l' m' else None
  | _ :: _, nil => None
  end.

Lemma strip_prefix_app : forall l r, strip_prefix l (l ++ r) = Some r.
Proof. induction l; intros; cbn; [ reflexivity | rewrite String.eqb_refl; auto ]. Qed.

Lemma strip_prefix_spec : forall l m r, strip_prefix l m = Some r -> m = l ++ r.
Proof.
  induction l as [| x l IH]; intros [| y m] r H; cbn in H; try discriminate;
    [ injection H as <-; reflexivity | injection H as <-; reflexivity |].
  destruct (String.eqb_spec x y) as [-> |]; [| discriminate ].
  cbn; f_equal; auto.
Qed.

Lemma strip_prefix_snoc : forall l x m r,
    strip_prefix (l ++ x :: nil) m = Some r -> strip_prefix l m = Some (x :: r).
Proof.
  intros * H; apply strip_prefix_spec in H; subst.
  rewrite <- List.app_assoc; apply strip_prefix_app.
Qed.

A global is named by X::Y::Z.a.b.c: the unit it lives in, by its path, then the chain of member selections inside it from the unit's root. Names are absolute, also inside the unit being elaborated: an open module is named by the same qualified name it will have once it is closed and its unit filed, so what a name denotes never depends on where it is read, and resolving it is a lookup with no re-expression.
A qualified name is not syntax: it is the key the global context resolves a chain of selections from a unit by, and the name a value of a global carries (dm_global, d_glob, ne_glob). q_chain is the chain, empty for the unit itself.
Record qname : Set := qname_mk
  { q_unit : path
  ; q_chain : list string }.

Definition qname_eq_dec : forall (x y : qname), {x = y} + {x <> y}.
Proof. decide equality; apply List.list_eq_dec, String.string_dec. Defined.

An abbreviation, not a definition: a rule keyed on q_abs then has a record literal in its conclusion, so inverting it yields equations that discriminate and injection see through.
Abbreviation q_abs fp ip := {| q_unit := fp; q_chain := ip |}.

The member x of the module mp.
Definition qname_in (mp : qname) (x : string) : qname :=
  {| q_unit := q_unit mp ; q_chain := q_chain mp ++ x :: nil |}.

The member chain ip of the module mp.
Definition qname_app (mp : qname) (ip : list string) : qname :=
  {| q_unit := q_unit mp ; q_chain := q_chain mp ++ ip |}.

Lemma qname_app_nil : forall p, qname_app p nil = p.
Proof. intros [u m]; unfold qname_app; cbn; rewrite List.app_nil_r; reflexivity. Qed.

The members of p inside the module mp, if p is in it.
Definition qname_strip (mp p : qname) : option (list string) :=
  if path_beq (q_unit mp) (q_unit p) then strip_prefix (q_chain mp) (q_chain p) else None.

Inductive Declarations

The declaration of a group of inductive types, as a unit stores it. It is generic in the sorts of terms E and context entries C so that it can be defined before them: gentry holds an ind_decl_g exp centry (ind_decl), and no syntactic operation looks inside it, since a declaration is always filed closed.
A group has members (imember_g): first the types it declares, in the order they are written (one for a single inductive type, several for a mutual block), then its views: the instances of types of groups filed before, at uniform arguments that mention a member, that its constructors nest through (as List 0l (Rose A) in Rose A := node (x : A) (ts : List 0l (Rose A))), in the order the command meets them. The members share the uniform parameters and the sort; each has its own non-uniform parameters and constructors.
  • ind_uparams is the telescope of the uniform parameters, innermost first, closed (the parameters of the enclosing frames outermost);
  • ind_sort is the universe every member lives in, a term over the uniform parameters;
  • ind_members lists the members.
The type former of member k is a_ind pq k, pq the path of the group, that of its first member's entry (ge_ind): every member is named by the group, so that the types of the constructors of one member may mention any other member before the entries of the others are filed.
The arguments of a constructor are stratified: a non-recursive argument ca_arg A has its type A over the non-recursive arguments before it and the member's parameters, and a recursive argument ca_rec t has a shape t (ptyp_g), whose components are over the non-recursive arguments before it and the member's parameters. Nothing may mention a recursive argument, so it occupies no binder of the arguments after it.
The shape of a recursive argument: the member k of the group at its non-uniform parameters Ps (pt_self k Ps), or a function from A to a shape (pt_pi A t).
Inductive ptyp_g (E : Set) : Set :=
The member k of the group at the non-uniform parameters Ps.
| pt_self : nat -> list E -> ptyp_g E
A function from the domain A into a shape, under one more binder.
| pt_pi : E -> ptyp_g E -> ptyp_g E.
Arguments pt_self {E}.
Arguments pt_pi {E}.

The non-uniform parameters at which a shape ends.
Fixpoint ptyp_ps {E : Set} (t : ptyp_g E) : list E :=
  match t with
  | pt_self _ Ps => Ps
  | pt_pi _ t => ptyp_ps t
  end.

The member a shape ends in.
Fixpoint ptyp_mem {E : Set} (t : ptyp_g E) : nat :=
  match t with
  | pt_self k _ => k
  | pt_pi _ t => ptyp_mem t
  end.

In stage A a shape is read by its parameters alone, so it stands for them wherever a list of terms is expected.
Coercion ptyp_ps : ptyp_g >-> list.

Inductive carg_g (E : Set) : Set :=
A non-recursive argument, of a type
| ca_arg : E -> carg_g E
A recursive argument, of a shape
| ca_rec : ptyp_g E -> carg_g E.
Arguments ca_arg {E}.
Arguments ca_rec {E}.

The head of a member: a declared type, by the canonical path of its own entry (mh_decl p), or a view (mh_view q k Is vm): the declared member k of the group filed at q, at the uniform arguments Is, terms over this group's uniform parameters in which this group's members occur, in normal form. A view of a member of q's group is one of all of them: vm lists, for each member of q's group in its order, the member of this group that is that member at Is (the k-th is the view itself). The eliminator at a view reads back as q's group's eliminator, whose blocks are those of these members.
Or a record view (mh_record q Is fl): the record type filed at q at the arguments Is, in which this group's members occur, stored as a view's, and the names fl of its fields, in order. A record view has one constructor, rview_con, whose arguments are the record's fields in order, classified as a constructor's arguments are; its elements are taken apart by projection. No eliminator eliminates at a record view: the record views come after every other member and have no block, and the recursive results of an argument of a record view are those of its fields (shape_leaves).
Inductive mhead_g (E : Set) : Set :=
A declared type, named by the canonical path of its own entry.
| mh_decl : qname -> mhead_g E
A view: the declared member k of the group at q at the uniform arguments Is, and the members vm of this group its group's members are at Is.
| mh_view : qname -> nat -> list E -> list nat -> mhead_g E
A record view: the record type at q at the arguments Is, its fields named fl.
| mh_record : qname -> list E -> list string -> mhead_g E.
Arguments mh_decl {E}.
Arguments mh_view {E}.
Arguments mh_record {E}.

The name of the one constructor of a record view: no identifier of the surface syntax (A-Za-z_A-Za-z0-9_*, the lexer's) is spelled so, so it can be neither written nor captured; the printer shows its elements as tuples of the record.
Definition rview_con : string := "(tuple)".

A member: its head, its non-uniform parameters (a telescope over the uniform ones, innermost first) and its constructors, in order, each with its arguments, outermost first. A view's are the filed ones of the member of q's group at Is, classified for this group: a recursive argument is one of a member of this group.
Record imember_g (E C : Set) : Set := mk_imember
  {
Whether the member is a declared type or a view, and of what.
    im_head : mhead_g E
  
The non-uniform parameters, over the group's uniform ones, innermost first.
  ; im_nparams : list C
  
The constructors in order, each with its arguments, outermost first.
  ; im_cons : list (string * list (carg_g E)) }.
Arguments mk_imember {E C}.
Arguments im_head {E C}.
Arguments im_nparams {E C}.
Arguments im_cons {E C}.

A group of inductive types: the uniform parameters all its members share, the one sort they are all of, and the members, the declared types in order, then the views.
Record ind_decl_g (E C : Set) : Set := mk_ind
  {
The uniform parameters, innermost first: the group's own, then those of the enclosing frames.
    ind_uparams : list C
  
The sort of every member, over the uniform parameters.
  ; ind_sort : E
  
The members: the declared types, then the views.
  ; ind_members : list (imember_g E C) }.
Arguments mk_ind {E C}.
Arguments ind_uparams {E C}.
Arguments ind_sort {E C}.
Arguments ind_members {E C}.

The declaration of a record type, filed by ge_record at its path, which names it. Records are never recursive: no field's type mentions the record.
Record record_decl_g (E C : Set) : Set := mk_record_decl
  {
The parameters, innermost first: the record's own, then those of the enclosing frames. A closed telescope.
    record_params : list C
  
The sort, over the parameters.
  ; record_sort : E
  
The fields in order, each named, its type over the fields before it (innermost first) and then the parameters.
  ; record_fields : list (string * E) }.
Arguments mk_record_decl {E C}.
Arguments record_params {E C}.
Arguments record_sort {E C}.
Arguments record_fields {E C}.

A block of an eliminator (a_elim), one per member of the group, in the group's order: eb_mk nm oZ A Bs. The motive A binds nm variables, the member's non-uniform parameters and the scrutinee; oZ is the type of the scrutinee as written, if it is written, over the non-uniform parameters; each branch (c, n, B) is the case of the constructor c, in order, and binds n variables: the non-uniform parameters, the arguments, and one recursive result per recursive argument.
Inductive eblock_g (E : Set) : Set :=
The block of nm motive binders, the written scrutinee type oZ, the motive A and the branches Bs.
| eb_mk : nat -> option E -> E -> list (string * nat * E) -> eblock_g E.
Arguments eb_mk {E}.
exp nests through blocks: with this scheme registered, its generated induction principle carries the hypotheses for a block's parts.
Scheme All for eblock_g.

The number of variables a block's motive binds.
Definition eb_nm {E : Set} (b : eblock_g E) : nat := match b with eb_mk nm _ _ _ => nm end.
A block's scrutinee type as written, if it is written.
Definition eb_ann {E : Set} (b : eblock_g E) : option E := match b with eb_mk _ oZ _ _ => oZ end.
A block's motive.
Definition eb_motive {E : Set} (b : eblock_g E) : E := match b with eb_mk _ _ A _ => A end.
A block's branches, one per constructor of its member, in order.
Definition eb_brs {E : Set} (b : eblock_g E) : list (string * nat * E) := match b with eb_mk _ _ _ Bs => Bs end.

Terms, Module Expressions and Units

Unlike a calculus of explicit substitutions, there is no constructor for substitution application and no syntactic category of substitutions. Weakenings and substitutions are meta-level operations (recursive functions on exp) defined further down in this file, and their algebraic laws are theorems (in Core.Syntactic.Substitution) rather than definitional equalities of the object theory.
The terms, and the module syntax nested in them. The two are one mutual family: a term binds a local module (a_let with b_mod) and selects members of module expressions (a_mem), and a module body contains terms.
  • modexp is a module expression: a unit me_unit, a local module slot me_var, a submodule me_mem, an argument me_app, or a literal unit me_lit. A literal is produced only by substitution, when ζ replaces a module slot by its unit.
  • gunit is a unit: its parameter telescope, innermost first, and its definition, a body or an alias. The definition is under the parameters.
  • gmod is a module body, newest entry last. Each named entry binds one index for the entries after it; a local open (gm_open), a pre-form the core expands before typing, binds one per item.
  • centry is a context entry: an assumption, a definition, or a module slot ce_mod U, which binds one index to the unit U.
The two ways a module's entries are stored: open (a local module) and closed (a filed module or an open frame).
Inductive smark : Set := sm_open | sm_closed.

Definition smark_eq_dec : forall (s s' : smark), {s = s'} + {s <> s'}.
Proof. decide equality. Defined.

The terms and the module syntax are one mutual family; its mutual principle syn_mut_ind below is written by hand, with one motive per sort that the hand-written cases share.
Inductive exp : Set :=
A large universe: a_typ n is Typeω²+n. It contains every small universe, and the large universes below it.
| a_typ : nat -> exp
A small universe, at a level: a_univ t is Type@{t}. The level is an arbitrary term of type Level, so a universe may be indexed by a variable, which is what makes universe polymorphism plain Π.
| a_univ : exp -> exp
The type of universe levels below ω·(n+1): a_level n is Level@n, and Level is Level@0, the finite levels. Levels are ordinary terms: a function may take and return them, so universe polymorphism is plain Π.
| a_level : nat -> exp
A level literal: a_llit (a, b) is the ordinal ω·a + b. The finite level n, a_llit (0, n), is written <n>l in the surface syntax.
| a_llit : o2 -> exp
The successor of a level
| a_succl : exp -> exp
The join of two levels
| a_maxl : exp -> exp -> exp
The token ℕ, written for the type bound by builtin natural: like a numeral (a_nlit), it is not a term of the typing judgment, and literal generation (Builtin) replaces it by the type former of the bound type.
| a_ntok : exp
The unit type, with η
| a_True : exp
Its element
| a_true : exp
The empty type
| a_False : exp
a_exfalso A M eliminates M into the motive A, which binds the scrutinee.
| a_exfalso : exp -> exp -> exp
The type former of the member k of the group pq of inductive types, to be applied to its parameters: pq names the group, the path of its first member's entry (ge_ind).
| a_ind : qname -> nat -> exp
The constructor c of the member k of the group pq, to be applied to the parameters and the arguments.
| a_con : qname -> nat -> string -> exp
A numeral as written. It is not a term of the typing judgment: literal generation (Builtin) replaces it by the chain of constructors of the inductive type bound as the natural numbers (builtin natural).
| a_nlit : nat -> exp
a_elim oq Us m Bks M eliminates M, of the member m of a group of inductive types, by the blocks Bks, one per member of the group in its order (eblock_g); the result is the motive of block m. The group is pq when oq = Some pq; when oq = None it is that of the scrutinee's type, the member m a declared one. The eliminator carries the group's uniform parameters Us: a stuck one is read at them.
| a_elim : option qname -> list exp -> nat -> list (eblock_g exp) -> exp -> exp
Functions: a_pi A B, B binding the argument
| a_pi : exp -> exp -> exp
a_fn A M, M binding the argument
| a_fn : exp -> exp -> exp
Application
| a_app : exp -> exp -> exp
Variable
| a_var : nat -> exp
Local binding: a_let b B binds #0 in B to the definition or the module b.
| a_let : bnd -> exp -> exp
The member x of the module H. A member of a global module is closed: X::Y::Z.W.bar stands for bar generalized over the parameters of every module enclosing it, outermost first, and is applied to them.
| a_mem : modexp -> string -> exp
The type former of the record filed at p, to be applied to its parameters
| a_record : qname -> exp
a_tuple T fs: the element of the record type T whose fields are fs, by name, in the declaration's order
| a_tuple : exp -> list (string * exp) -> exp
a_proj f M: the field f of M, of a record type
| a_proj : string -> exp -> exp
with modexp : Set :=
A unit, by its path
| me_unit : path -> modexp
A local module slot
| me_var : nat -> modexp
A submodule
| me_mem : modexp -> string -> modexp
A module applied to one more argument
| me_app : modexp -> exp -> modexp
A unit given literally; only substitution produces one
| me_lit : gunit -> modexp
with bnd : Set :=
b_def oA M: a definition, of the type A when oA = Some A, and of a type it infers when oA = None
| b_def : option exp -> exp -> bnd
b_mod U: a local module
| b_mod : gunit -> bnd
with gunit : Set :=
gu_mk Δ D: the parameters, innermost first, and the definition under them
| gu_mk : list centry -> moddef -> gunit
with moddef : Set :=
A body, stored open (a local module: its entries mention the parameters and the entries before them) or closed (a filed module or an open frame: every entry is closed over the module's full telescope)
| md_body : smark -> gmod -> moddef
An alias of a module expression
| md_alias : modexp -> moddef
with gmod : Set :=
The empty body
| gm_nil : gmod
A named entry after the body before it
| gm_ext : gmod -> string -> gentry -> gmod
gm_open Φ H items: a local open. It binds one index per item, the entries its items generate (items_gen); every reader of the body reads it as those entries (body_xp).
| gm_open : gmod -> modexp -> list iitem -> gmod
with gentry : Set :=
ge_def b pv A B: b says whether the definition is transparent, pv whether it is private, and B is None for an axiom. A filed definition is closed; a definition of a local body is read in the body's context.
| ge_def : bool -> bool -> exp -> option exp -> gentry
ge_mod pv U: a submodule, private when pv
| ge_mod : bool -> gunit -> gentry
ge_ind pv pq k D Φ: the declared member k of the group D of inductive types, private when pv: the group's path pq (the path of the entry of member 0), and the body Φ of the member's module, whose members are its constructors (and the recursor), under the uniform parameters of D (ind_unit). As a term the entry is the type former a_ind pq k.
| ge_ind : bool -> qname -> nat -> ind_decl_g exp centry -> gmod -> gentry
ge_def_mod pv A M U: a definition with a module part, private when pv: as a term, the transparent definition of type A equal to M; as a module, the unit U. An inductive or record alias, or an open's item naming a type former, is one: M is the alias's target read as a term and U the alias of it, both over the alias's full telescope. A filed one is closed.
| ge_def_mod : bool -> exp -> exp -> gunit -> gentry
ge_record pv p R Φ: the record type declared by R, private when pv, at its own path p, and the body Φ of its module, under the record's parameters and then a value of the record at them (record_mod_tele). As a term the entry is the type former a_record p.
| ge_record : bool -> qname -> record_decl_g exp centry -> gmod -> gentry
with centry : Set :=
An assumption of a type
| ce_ass : exp -> centry
ce_def A M: a definition of type A
| ce_def : exp -> exp -> centry
A module slot, holding the unit
| ce_mod : gunit -> centry
ce_dm A M U: a definition with a module part, the local ge_def_mod: a definition of type A equal to M and a module slot holding U, at one index
| ce_dm : exp -> exp -> gunit -> centry.

Abbreviation typ := exp.
Abbreviation carg := (carg_g exp).
Abbreviation ptyp := (ptyp_g exp).
Abbreviation ind_decl := (ind_decl_g exp centry).
Abbreviation record_decl := (record_decl_g exp centry).
Abbreviation imember := (imember_g exp centry).
Abbreviation mhead := (mhead_g exp).
Abbreviation eblock := (eblock_g exp).

A property of every branch of an eliminator, under its binders. A structural recursion on the list, so that a recursive function on terms may use it on the branches' bodies.
Fixpoint all_brs {A : Type} (f : nat -> A -> Prop) (Bs : list (string * nat * A)) : Prop :=
  match Bs with
  | nil => True
  | b :: Bs' => f (snd (fst b)) (snd b) /\ all_brs f Bs'
  end.

A property of every block of an eliminator: of its binder count, its annotation, its motive and its branches.
Fixpoint all_blocks {A : Set} (f : nat -> option A -> A -> list (string * nat * A) -> Prop) (Bks : list (eblock_g A)) : Prop :=
  match Bks with
  | nil => True
  | eb_mk nm oZ M Bs :: Bks' => f nm oZ M Bs /\ all_blocks f Bks'
  end.

The annotation of a block, scoped as f says, when there is one.
Definition opt_all {A : Set} (f : A -> Prop) (o : option A) : Prop :=
  match o with Some a => f a | None => True end.

Each element of a list as f says (the uniform parameters an eliminator carries).
Fixpoint all_list {A : Set} (f : A -> Prop) (l : list A) : Prop :=
  match l with
  | nil => True
  | x :: l' => f x /\ all_list f l'
  end.

Lemma all_brs_Forall : forall {A : Type} (f : nat -> A -> Prop) Bs,
    all_brs f Bs <-> List.Forall (fun b => f (snd (fst b)) (snd b)) Bs.
Proof.
  induction Bs as [| b Bs IH]; cbn; [ split; auto |].
  rewrite IH; split; [ intros []; constructor; assumption | intros H; inversion H; auto ].
Qed.

all_brs and all_blocks are all_list at the branch and at the block.
Lemma all_brs_all_list : forall {A : Set} (f : nat -> A -> Prop) Bs,
    all_brs f Bs <-> all_list (fun b => f (snd (fst b)) (snd b)) Bs.
Proof. induction Bs as [| b Bs IH]; cbn; [ reflexivity | rewrite IH; reflexivity ]. Qed.

Lemma all_blocks_all_list : forall {A : Set} (f : nat -> option A -> A -> list (string * nat * A) -> Prop) Bks,
    all_blocks f Bks <-> all_list (fun b => match b with eb_mk nm oZ M Bs => f nm oZ M Bs end) Bks.
Proof. induction Bks as [| [] Bks IH]; cbn; [ reflexivity | rewrite IH; reflexivity ]. Qed.

Lemma all_list_Forall : forall {A : Set} (f : A -> Prop) l, all_list f l <-> List.Forall f l.
Proof.
  induction l as [| x l IH]; cbn; split; intros H; auto.
  - destruct H as [H1 H2]; constructor; [ exact H1 | apply IH; exact H2 ].
  - inversion H; subst; split; [ assumption | apply IH; assumption ].
Qed.

Induction

The family is nested through list centry and option exp, so its induction principle is written by hand. syn_mut_ind has one motive per sort; a telescope carries Forall of the entry motive, and a definition body the motive of every expression it may hold.
Section syn_mut_ind.
  Variables (Pe : exp -> Prop) (Pm : modexp -> Prop) (Pb : bnd -> Prop)
    (Pu : gunit -> Prop) (Pd : moddef -> Prop) (Pg : gmod -> Prop)
    (Pn : gentry -> Prop) (Pc : centry -> Prop).

  Hypotheses
    (case_typ : forall i, Pe (a_typ i))
    (case_univ : forall t, Pe t -> Pe (a_univ t))
    (case_level : forall n, Pe (a_level n))
    (case_llit : forall n, Pe (a_llit n))
    (case_succl : forall M, Pe M -> Pe (a_succl M))
    (case_maxl : forall M N, Pe M -> Pe N -> Pe (a_maxl M N))
    (case_ntok : Pe a_ntok)
    (case_True : Pe a_True)
    (case_true : Pe a_true)
    (case_False : Pe a_False)
    (case_exfalso : forall A M, Pe A -> Pe M -> Pe (a_exfalso A M))
    (case_ind : forall p k, Pe (a_ind p k))
    (case_con : forall p k c, Pe (a_con p k c))
    (case_nlit : forall n, Pe (a_nlit n))
    (case_elim : forall oq Us m Bks M,
        List.Forall Pe Us ->
        List.Forall (fun b => (forall Z, eb_ann b = Some Z -> Pe Z) /\ Pe (eb_motive b) /\
                              List.Forall (fun br => Pe (snd br)) (eb_brs b)) Bks ->
        Pe M -> Pe (a_elim oq Us m Bks M))
    (case_pi : forall A B, Pe A -> Pe B -> Pe (a_pi A B))
    (case_fn : forall A M, Pe A -> Pe M -> Pe (a_fn A M))
    (case_app : forall M N, Pe M -> Pe N -> Pe (a_app M N))
    (case_var : forall x, Pe (a_var x))
    (case_let : forall b B, Pb b -> Pe B -> Pe (a_let b B))
    (case_mem : forall H x, Pm H -> Pe (a_mem H x))
    (case_record : forall p, Pe (a_record p))
    (case_tuple : forall T fs, Pe T -> List.Forall (fun f => Pe (snd f)) fs -> Pe (a_tuple T fs))
    (case_proj : forall f M, Pe M -> Pe (a_proj f M))
    (case_me_unit : forall fp, Pm (me_unit fp))
    (case_me_var : forall k, Pm (me_var k))
    (case_me_mem : forall H y, Pm H -> Pm (me_mem H y))
    (case_me_app : forall H N, Pm H -> Pe N -> Pm (me_app H N))
    (case_me_lit : forall U, Pu U -> Pm (me_lit U))
    (case_b_def : forall oA M, (forall A, oA = Some A -> Pe A) -> Pe M -> Pb (b_def oA M))
    (case_b_mod : forall U, Pu U -> Pb (b_mod U))
    (case_gu_mk : forall Δ D, List.Forall Pc Δ -> Pd D -> Pu (gu_mk Δ D))
    (case_md_body : forall s Φ, Pg Φ -> Pd (md_body s Φ))
    (case_md_alias : forall E, Pm E -> Pd (md_alias E))
    (case_gm_nil : Pg gm_nil)
    (case_gm_ext : forall Φ x E, Pg Φ -> Pn E -> Pg (gm_ext Φ x E))
    (case_gm_open : forall Φ H its, Pg Φ -> Pm H -> Pg (gm_open Φ H its))
    (case_ge_def : forall b pv A B, Pe A -> (forall M, B = Some M -> Pe M) -> Pn (ge_def b pv A B))
    (case_ge_mod : forall pv U, Pu U -> Pn (ge_mod pv U))
    (case_ge_ind : forall pv p k D Φ, Pg Φ -> Pn (ge_ind pv p k D Φ))
    (case_ge_def_mod : forall pv A M U, Pe A -> Pe M -> Pu U -> Pn (ge_def_mod pv A M U))
    (case_ge_record : forall pv p R Φ, Pg Φ -> Pn (ge_record pv p R Φ))
    (case_ce_ass : forall A, Pe A -> Pc (ce_ass A))
    (case_ce_def : forall A M, Pe A -> Pe M -> Pc (ce_def A M))
    (case_ce_mod : forall U, Pu U -> Pc (ce_mod U))
    (case_ce_dm : forall A M U, Pe A -> Pe M -> Pu U -> Pc (ce_dm A M U)).

The mutual induction principle on terms, written by hand: the branches of an eliminator's blocks are nested through pairs.
  Fixpoint exp_mut (M : exp) : Pe M :=
    match M with
    | a_typ i => case_typ i
    | a_univ t => case_univ t (exp_mut t)
    | a_level n => case_level n
    | a_llit n => case_llit n
    | a_succl M => case_succl M (exp_mut M)
    | a_maxl M N => case_maxl M N (exp_mut M) (exp_mut N)
    | a_ntok => case_ntok
    | a_True => case_True
    | a_true => case_true
    | a_False => case_False
    | a_exfalso A M => case_exfalso A M (exp_mut A) (exp_mut M)
    | a_ind p k => case_ind p k
    | a_con p k c => case_con p k c
    | a_nlit n => case_nlit n
    | a_elim oq Us0 m Bks M =>
        case_elim oq Us0 m Bks M
          ((fix us_mut (Us : list exp) : List.Forall Pe Us :=
              match Us with
              | nil => List.Forall_nil _
              | cons U Us' => List.Forall_cons U (exp_mut U) (us_mut Us')
              end) Us0)
          ((fix blocks_mut (Bks : list eblock) :
              List.Forall (fun b => (forall Z, eb_ann b = Some Z -> Pe Z) /\ Pe (eb_motive b) /\
                                    List.Forall (fun br => Pe (snd br)) (eb_brs b)) Bks :=
              match Bks with
              | nil => List.Forall_nil _
              | cons (eb_mk nm oZ A Bs) Bks' =>
                  List.Forall_cons (eb_mk nm oZ A Bs)
                    (conj
                       (match oZ as o return (forall Z, o = Some Z -> Pe Z) with
                        | Some Z0 => fun Z e => match e in _ = o' return match o' with Some Z => Pe Z | None => True end with
                                               | eq_refl => exp_mut Z0 end
                        | None => fun Z e => False_ind _ (match e in _ = o' return match o' with Some _ => False | None => True end with
                                             | eq_refl => I end)
                        end)
                       (conj (exp_mut A)
                          ((fix brs_mut (Bs : list (string * nat * exp)) : List.Forall (fun b => Pe (snd b)) Bs :=
                              match Bs with
                              | nil => List.Forall_nil _
                              | cons b Bs' => List.Forall_cons b (exp_mut (snd b)) (brs_mut Bs')
                              end) Bs)))
                    (blocks_mut Bks')
              end) Bks)
          (exp_mut M)
    | a_pi A B => case_pi A B (exp_mut A) (exp_mut B)
    | a_fn A M => case_fn A M (exp_mut A) (exp_mut M)
    | a_app M N => case_app M N (exp_mut M) (exp_mut N)
    | a_var x => case_var x
    | a_let b B => case_let b B (bnd_mut b) (exp_mut B)
    | a_mem H x => case_mem H x (modexp_mut H)
    | a_record p => case_record p
    | a_tuple T fs0 =>
        case_tuple T fs0 (exp_mut T)
          ((fix fields_mut (fs : list (string * exp)) : List.Forall (fun f => Pe (snd f)) fs :=
              match fs with
              | nil => List.Forall_nil _
              | cons f fs' => List.Forall_cons f (exp_mut (snd f)) (fields_mut fs')
              end) fs0)
    | a_proj f M => case_proj f M (exp_mut M)
    end
  with modexp_mut (H : modexp) : Pm H :=
    match H with
    | me_unit fp => case_me_unit fp
    | me_var k => case_me_var k
    | me_mem H y => case_me_mem H y (modexp_mut H)
    | me_app H N => case_me_app H N (modexp_mut H) (exp_mut N)
    | me_lit U => case_me_lit U (gunit_mut U)
    end
  with bnd_mut (b : bnd) : Pb b :=
    match b with
    | b_def oA M =>
        case_b_def oA M
          (match oA as o return (forall A, o = Some A -> Pe A) with
           | Some A0 => fun A e => match e in _ = o' return match o' with Some A => Pe A | None => True end with
                                  | eq_refl => exp_mut A0 end
           | None => fun A e => False_ind _ (match e in _ = o' return match o' with Some _ => False | None => True end with
                                | eq_refl => I end)
           end)
          (exp_mut M)
    | b_mod U => case_b_mod U (gunit_mut U)
    end
  with gunit_mut (U : gunit) : Pu U :=
    match U with
    | gu_mk Δ D =>
        case_gu_mk Δ D
          ((fix tele_mut (Δ : list centry) : List.Forall Pc Δ :=
              match Δ with
              | nil => List.Forall_nil _
              | cons e Δ' => List.Forall_cons _ (centry_mut e) (tele_mut Δ')
              end) Δ)
          (moddef_mut D)
    end
  with moddef_mut (D : moddef) : Pd D :=
    match D with
    | md_body s Φ => case_md_body s Φ (gmod_mut Φ)
    | md_alias E => case_md_alias E (modexp_mut E)
    end
  with gmod_mut (Φ : gmod) : Pg Φ :=
    match Φ with
    | gm_nil => case_gm_nil
    | gm_ext Φ x E => case_gm_ext Φ x E (gmod_mut Φ) (gentry_mut E)
    | gm_open Φ H its => case_gm_open Φ H its (gmod_mut Φ) (modexp_mut H)
    end
  with gentry_mut (E : gentry) : Pn E :=
    match E with
    | ge_def b pv A B =>
        case_ge_def b pv A B (exp_mut A)
          (match B as o return (forall M, o = Some M -> Pe M) with
           | Some M0 => fun M e => match e in _ = o' return match o' with Some M => Pe M | None => True end with
                                  | eq_refl => exp_mut M0 end
           | None => fun M e => False_ind _ (match e in _ = o' return match o' with Some _ => False | None => True end with
                                | eq_refl => I end)
           end)
    | ge_mod pv U => case_ge_mod pv U (gunit_mut U)
    | ge_ind pv p k D Φ => case_ge_ind pv p k D Φ (gmod_mut Φ)
    | ge_def_mod pv A M U => case_ge_def_mod pv A M U (exp_mut A) (exp_mut M) (gunit_mut U)
    | ge_record pv p R Φ => case_ge_record pv p R Φ (gmod_mut Φ)
    end
  with centry_mut (e : centry) : Pc e :=
    match e with
    | ce_ass A => case_ce_ass A (exp_mut A)
    | ce_def A M => case_ce_def A M (exp_mut A) (exp_mut M)
    | ce_mod U => case_ce_mod U (gunit_mut U)
    | ce_dm A M U => case_ce_dm A M U (exp_mut A) (exp_mut M) (gunit_mut U)
    end.

  Theorem syn_mut_ind :
    (forall M, Pe M) /\ (forall H, Pm H) /\ (forall b, Pb b) /\ (forall U, Pu U) /\
    (forall D, Pd D) /\ (forall Φ, Pg Φ) /\ (forall E, Pn E) /\
    (forall e, Pc e).
  Proof.
    repeat split; [ exact exp_mut | exact modexp_mut | exact bnd_mut | exact gunit_mut
                  | exact moddef_mut | exact gmod_mut | exact gentry_mut
                  | exact centry_mut ].
  Qed.
End syn_mut_ind.

Chains of Selections

H.y1. … .yn, the submodules pre selected from H in order.
Fixpoint me_mems (H : modexp) (pre : list string) : modexp :=
  match pre with
  | nil => H
  | y :: pre' => me_mems (me_mem H y) pre'
  end.

H.y1. … .yn.x as a term: submodule selections, then a member.
Fixpoint member_ref (H : modexp) (ch : list string) : exp :=
  match ch with
  | nil => a_true
  | x :: nil => a_mem H x
  | y :: ch' => member_ref (me_mem H y) ch'
  end.

The module named X::Y.W.Z, q_abs ["X"; "Y"] ["W"; "Z"], and the global named so, both as selections from the unit. H N1 … Nn: a module applied to arguments.
Fixpoint me_apps (H : modexp) (Ns : list exp) : modexp :=
  match Ns with
  | nil => H
  | N :: Ns' => me_apps (me_app H N) Ns'
  end.

A module expression read as the term it spells, as written: a selection is the member as a term, an application the term applied; a unit, a module slot and a literal spell no term.
Fixpoint modexp_as_term (H : modexp) : option exp :=
  match H with
  | me_mem H' y => Some (a_mem H' y)
  | me_app H' N => option_map (fun M => a_app M N) (modexp_as_term H')
  | _ => None
  end.

Definition qname_mod (p : qname) : modexp := me_mems (me_unit (q_unit p)) (q_chain p).

Definition qname_term (p : qname) : exp := member_ref (me_unit (q_unit p)) (q_chain p).

The qualified name a chain of selections from a unit spells, and None for any other module expression.
Fixpoint mod_qname (H : modexp) : option qname :=
  match H with
  | me_unit fp => Some (q_abs fp nil)
  | me_mem H y =>
      match mod_qname H with
      | Some p => Some {| q_unit := q_unit p; q_chain := q_chain p ++ y :: nil |}
      | None => None
      end
  | _ => None
  end.

Units

A body unit and a body entry, the forms every global module has.
Abbreviation gu_body Δ Φ := (gu_mk Δ (md_body sm_closed Φ)).
Abbreviation ge_body pv Δ Φ := (ge_mod pv (gu_body Δ Φ)).
A local (open) body unit.
Abbreviation gu_open Δ Φ := (gu_mk Δ (md_body sm_open Φ)).

Definition gu_params (U : gunit) : list centry := match U with gu_mk Δ _ => Δ end.

The number of uniform parameters of a group.
Definition ind_nu (D : ind_decl) : nat := List.length (ind_uparams D).

The member k of a group.
Definition ind_member (D : ind_decl) (k : nat) : option imember := List.nth_error (ind_members D) k.

The parameters of a member, innermost first: its non-uniform ones inside the group's uniform ones; their numbers.
Definition im_params (D : ind_decl) (M : imember) : list centry := im_nparams M ++ ind_uparams D.
The number of a member's non-uniform parameters.
Definition im_nn (M : imember) : nat := List.length (im_nparams M).
The number of all a member's parameters, uniform and non-uniform.
Definition im_np (D : ind_decl) (M : imember) : nat := im_nn M + ind_nu D.

A declared member, and the path of its entry.
Definition im_path (M : imember) : option qname :=
  match im_head M with mh_decl p => Some p | _ => None end.

The module of the inductive type D of body Φ, as a unit: it takes the uniform parameters, with the frames' parameters outside them, so that it is closed, as an alias is.
Definition ind_unit (D : ind_decl) (Φ : gmod) : gunit := gu_body (ind_uparams D) Φ.

Definition gu_def (U : gunit) : moddef := match U with gu_mk _ D => D end.

The body of a body unit, and the empty body for an alias.
Definition gu_mod (U : gunit) : gmod :=
  match U with
  | gu_mk _ (md_body _ Φ) => Φ
  | gu_mk _ (md_alias _) => gm_nil
  end.

The number of indices a body binds.
Fixpoint gm_binders (Φ : gmod) : nat :=
  match Φ with
  | gm_nil => 0
  | gm_ext Φ' _ _ => S (gm_binders Φ')
  | gm_open Φ' _ its => List.length its + gm_binders Φ'
  end.

The name an import item declares.
Definition iitem_name (it : iitem) : string := let '(_, d, _) := it in d.

The names Φ declares, outermost last, and a name not among them.
Fixpoint gm_names (Φ : gmod) : list string :=
  match Φ with
  | gm_nil => nil
  | gm_ext Φ' x _ => x :: gm_names Φ'
  | gm_open Φ' _ its => rev (map iitem_name its) ++ gm_names Φ'
  end.

Definition gm_fresh (x : string) (Φ : gmod) : Prop :=
  ~ List.In x (gm_names Φ).

Notations

Every notation of the syntax lives in ordinary constr, in mctt_scope: there is no custom entry and hence no delimiter to write. The price is that a spelling can denote only one sort, so the normal forms, which mirror the expressions constructor for constructor, carry a superscript ⁿ. Values carry a superscript ᵈ; see Domain_Notations. The notations of each topic are in their own module, after its definitions; Syntax_Notations, at the end, exports all of them but those of module bodies (GlobalCtx_Notations) and of weakenings (Wk_Notations).
Everything that reads as an atom is at level 0, the postfix forms at level 1, and the constructor forms with a recursive last argument at level 2.
Module Exp_Notations.
A large universe, a_typ n, is Typeω@n: it is the universe ω²+n, above every small one.
  Notation "'Typeω' @ n" := (a_typ n) (at level 1, n at level 0, format "'Typeω' @ n") : mctt_scope.
A small universe at an arbitrary level term, and — for a literal level — the short form the literal-level rules are written with.
  Notation "'Type' ⟨ t ⟩" := (a_univ t) (at level 0, t at level 99, format "'Type' ⟨ t ⟩") : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'Type' @ n" := (a_univ (a_llit (ofin n))) (at level 1, n at level 0, format "'Type' @ n") : mctt_scope.
Level@n is the type of levels below ω·(n+1), and Level the finite ones, Level@0: Level is declared second so that it is the spelling a level type of sort 0 prints with.
  Notation "'Level' @ n" := (a_level n) (at level 1, n at level 0, format "'Level' @ n") : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'Level'" := (a_level 0) : mctt_scope.
The level literals: 𝕃ᵒ o is the ordinal o, and 𝕃@n the finite level n, the surface syntax's <n>l. The token is not a word: lv would make every identifier of that name a keyword.
  Notation "'𝕃ᵒ' o" := (a_llit o) (at level 1, o at level 0, format "'𝕃ᵒ' o") : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'𝕃' @ n" := (a_llit (ofin n)) (at level 1, n at level 0, format "'𝕃' @ n") : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'succl' M" := (a_succl M) (at level 2, M at level 1) : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'maxl' M N" := (a_maxl M N) (at level 2, M at level 1, N at level 1) : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'#' n" := (a_var n) (at level 1, n at level 0, format "'#' n") : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'ℕ'" := a_ntok : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'λ' A M" := (a_fn A M) (at level 2, A at level 1, M at level 60) : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'Π' A B" := (a_pi A B) (at level 2, A at level 1, B at level 60) : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'ℓ' A ≔ M 'in' B" := (a_let (b_def (Some A) M) B) (at level 2, A at level 1, M at level 60, B at level 60) : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'ℓ' ≔ M 'in' B" := (a_let (b_def None M) B) (at level 2, M at level 60, B at level 60) : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'ℓₘ' U 'in' B" := (a_let (b_mod U) B) (at level 2, U at level 1, B at level 60) : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'⊤'" := a_True : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'⋆'" := a_true : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'⊥'" := a_False : mctt_scope.
  Notation "'efq' M 'return' A" := (a_exfalso A M) (at level 2, M at level 60, A at level 60) : mctt_scope.
Application needs an explicit operator: a constr notation may not be pure juxtaposition, which is Rocq's own application.
  Notation "M $ N" := (a_app M N) (at level 10, left associativity) : mctt_scope.
End Exp_Notations.

A module body: ⋄ is empty, and Φ ⊳ x ↦ E adds the entry E named x.
Module GlobalCtx_Notations.
  Notation "⋄" := gm_nil.
  Notation "Φ ⊳ x ↦ E" := (gm_ext Φ x E) (at level 50, x at level 0).
End GlobalCtx_Notations.

Contexts

A context entry occupies one de Bruijn index, whether it is an assumption, a definition or a module slot.
Abbreviation ctx := (list centry).

A body as the context entries it binds, innermost first. A local open binds one placeholder per item: a pre-form is never typed. So does an inductive type, which only a filed module declares.
Fixpoint body_ctx (Φ : gmod) : ctx :=
  match Φ with
  | gm_nil => nil
  | gm_ext Φ' _ (ge_def _ _ A (Some M)) => cons (ce_def A M) (body_ctx Φ')
  | gm_ext Φ' _ (ge_def _ _ A None) => cons (ce_ass A) (body_ctx Φ')
  | gm_ext Φ' _ (ge_mod _ U) => cons (ce_mod U) (body_ctx Φ')
  | gm_ext Φ' _ (ge_ind _ _ _ _ _) => cons (ce_ass a_True) (body_ctx Φ')
  | gm_ext Φ' _ (ge_def_mod _ A M U) => cons (ce_dm A M U) (body_ctx Φ')
  | gm_ext Φ' _ (ge_record _ _ _ _) => cons (ce_ass a_True) (body_ctx Φ')
  | gm_open Φ' _ its => List.repeat (ce_ass a_True) (List.length its) ++ body_ctx Φ'
  end.

The term part of a body's entry, its type and its body: a definition with a body, or a definition with a module part.
Definition entry_tm (E : gentry) : option (exp * exp) :=
  match E with
  | ge_def _ _ A (Some M) => Some (A, M)
  | ge_def_mod _ A M _ => Some (A, M)
  | _ => None
  end.

The module part of a body's entry, its unit: a module, or a definition with a module part.
Definition entry_unit (E : gentry) : option gunit :=
  match E with
  | ge_mod _ U => Some U
  | ge_def_mod _ _ _ U => Some U
  | _ => None
  end.

The unit a context entry holds: a module slot's, or a definition with a module part's.
Definition centry_unit (e : centry) : option gunit :=
  match e with
  | ce_mod U | ce_dm _ _ U => Some U
  | _ => None
  end.

Notations

Module Ctx_Notations.
Extension is ▹ rather than the paper's comma: a parsing , in constr would steal Rocq's pair notation. Both are restricted to centry so that an unrelated list does not print as a context. A definition entry is Γ ▸ A ≔ M; it has its own first token because Γ ▹ A would otherwise be a proper prefix of it.
  Notation "⋅" := (@nil centry) : mctt_scope.
  Notation "Γ ▹ A" := (@cons centry (ce_ass A) Γ) (at level 50, left associativity) : mctt_scope.
  Notation "Γ ▸ A ≔ M" := (@cons centry (ce_def A M) Γ) (at level 50, left associativity) : mctt_scope.
  Notation "Γ '▹ₘ' U" := (@cons centry (ce_mod U) Γ) (at level 50, left associativity) : mctt_scope.
  Notation "Γ '▸ₘ' A ≔ M ‖ U" := (@cons centry (ce_dm A M U) Γ) (at level 50, left associativity) : mctt_scope.
End Ctx_Notations.

Universe Indices

The universes of the model form two tiers:
  • the small tier us o, indexed by an ordinal o below ω² (see Core.Syntactic.Levels.Ordinals), whose universes are the small universes 𝕌@l whose levels realise an ordinal below o;
  • the large tier ul n (the syntactic Typeω@n, read as Typeω²+n), whose universes are every small universe and the large ones 𝕌ω@m for m < n.
Every small index is below every large one. The large tier is the default: ul is a coercion, so per_univ_elem i for a natural number i is the large universe Typeω²+i.
Inductive universe_index : Set :=
| us : o2 -> universe_index
| ul : nat -> universe_index.

Coercion ul : nat >-> universe_index.

Definition universe_index_lt (u v : universe_index) : Prop :=
  match u, v with
  | us j, us k => ordinal_lt j k
  | us _, ul _ => True
  | ul _, us _ => False
  | ul j, ul k => j < k
  end.

Definition universe_index_le (u v : universe_index) : Prop :=
  match u, v with
  | us j, us k => ordinal_le j k
  | us _, ul _ => True
  | ul _, us _ => False
  | ul j, ul k => j <= k
  end.

Lemma universe_index_lt_le_trans : forall u v w, universe_index_lt u v -> universe_index_le v w -> universe_index_lt u w.
Proof. intros [] [] []; cbn; intros; auto; try lia; ord. Qed.

Lemma universe_index_le_refl : forall u, universe_index_le u u.
Proof. intros []; cbn; [ ord | lia ]. Qed.

Lemma universe_index_le_trans : forall u v w, universe_index_le u v -> universe_index_le v w -> universe_index_le u w.
Proof. intros [] [] []; cbn; intros; auto; try lia; ord. Qed.

Lemma universe_index_lt_le : forall u v, universe_index_lt u v -> universe_index_le u v.
Proof. intros [] []; cbn; intros; auto; try lia; ord. Qed.

Lemma universe_index_wf : well_founded universe_index_lt.
Proof.
  assert (Hs : forall j, Acc universe_index_lt (us j)).
  { intros j; induction j as [j IH] using (well_founded_ind ordinal_lt_wf).
    constructor; intros [k | k] Hk; cbn in Hk; [ apply IH; exact Hk | contradiction ]. }
  intros [j | n]; [ apply Hs |].
  induction n as [n IH] using lt_wf_ind; constructor; intros [k | k] Hk; cbn in Hk; [ apply Hs | apply IH; exact Hk ].
Qed.

Universes at Any Index, as Terms and Values

A judgment in a universe is the four-value pattern of its two sides in the universe's element PER, whichever tier the universe is in. The lemmas are stated at an index u, through the universe's term universe_index_term u and value universe_index_value u; the large forms below are their instances at ul i, which is Typeω@i by computation.
Definition universe_index_term (u : universe_index) : exp :=
  match u with us o => a_univ (a_llit o) | ul n => a_typ n end.

A large level whose universe contains the universe at u.
Definition large_level_above (u : universe_index) : nat :=
  match u with us _ => 0 | ul n => S n end.

The large level a type at u is also a type of.
Definition large_level (u : universe_index) : nat :=
  match u with us _ => 0 | ul n => n end.

Lemma universe_index_lt_large_level_above : forall u, universe_index_lt u (large_level_above u).
Proof. intros []; cbn; [ exact I | lia ]. Qed.

Lemma universe_index_le_large_level : forall u, universe_index_le u (large_level u).
Proof. intros []; cbn; [ exact I | lia ]. Qed.

The least index: Type@0 is below every universe.
Lemma universe_index_le_least : forall u, universe_index_le (us ordinal_zero) u.
Proof. intros []; cbn; [ ord | exact I ]. Qed.

The large levels of two ordered indices are ordered: a small universe lives in Typeω@0, and the large tier's order is the order on levels.
Lemma universe_index_le_large_level_le : forall u v, universe_index_le u v -> large_level u <= large_level v.
Proof. intros [] []; cbn; intros; lia. Qed.

The join of two indices: a large universe absorbs a small one.
Definition universe_index_max (u v : universe_index) : universe_index :=
  match u, v with
  | us n, us m => us (ordinal_max n m)
  | us _, ul i => ul i
  | ul i, us _ => ul i
  | ul i, ul j => ul (max i j)
  end.

Lemma universe_index_le_universe_index_max_left : forall u v, universe_index_le u (universe_index_max u v).
Proof. intros [] []; cbn; try exact I; try lia; ord. Qed.

Lemma universe_index_le_universe_index_max_right : forall u v, universe_index_le v (universe_index_max u v).
Proof. intros [] []; cbn; try exact I; try lia; ord. Qed.

Lemma universe_index_max_lub : forall u v w, universe_index_le u w -> universe_index_le v w -> universe_index_le (universe_index_max u v) w.
Proof. intros [] [] []; cbn; intros; try contradiction; try exact I; try lia; ord. Qed.

Discharges the order side conditions between universe indices.
Ltac solve_universe_index :=
  first [ assumption | exact I | solve [ cbn [universe_index_lt universe_index_le] in *; lia ]
        | solve [ cbn [universe_index_lt universe_index_le] in *; ord ]
        | solve [ repeat match goal with k : universe_index |- _ => destruct k end;
                  cbn [universe_index_lt universe_index_le] in *; first [ contradiction | exact I | lia | ord ] ] ].

Levels as Expressions

A flat level max (c, k₁ + a₁, …, kₙ + aₙ) is written as an expression by folding maxl to the left over the atoms, each under its own offset of succls. The constant is written only when it is not 0: with atoms present, 𝕃@0 is the neutral element of maxl and would not be a normal form. This is the spelling of a canonical level normal form (nf_lvl below), so it is also how a level is printed.
Fixpoint succl_n (k : nat) (M : exp) : exp :=
  match k with
  | 0 => M
  | S k' => a_succl (succl_n k' M)
  end.

Fixpoint lvl_fold (hd : exp) (xs : list (nat * exp)) : exp :=
  match xs with
  | nil => hd
  | (k, a) :: r => lvl_fold (a_maxl hd (succl_n k a)) r
  end.

Definition lvl_exp_of (c : o2) (xs : list (nat * exp)) : exp :=
  match xs, c with
  | nil, _ => a_llit c
  | (k, a) :: r, (0, 0) => lvl_fold (succl_n k a) r
  | (k, a) :: r, _ => lvl_fold (a_maxl (a_llit c) (succl_n k a)) r
  end.

Normal and Neutral Forms

Normal forms nest through lists, as terms do: the parameters and arguments of a type former or a constructor are a list nf; the atoms of a canonical level, and the blocks and branches of a stuck eliminator, are lists of the small records below, generic in what they hold. Each record has Scheme All registered, so that the induction principle generated for nf and ne carries hypotheses for what they hold, as list_all does for lists.
An atom k + a of a canonical level: the neutral level a, of type Level@s, with its offset k.
Record level_atom_g (E : Set) : Set := mk_level_atom
  {
The offset k: the number of successors above the neutral
    atom_offset : nat
    
The sort s of the neutral: it is of type Level@s, so below ω·(s+1)
  ; atom_sort : nat
    
The neutral level a
  ; atom_level : E }.
Arguments mk_level_atom {E}.
Arguments atom_offset {E}.
Arguments atom_sort {E}.
Arguments atom_level {E}.
Scheme All for level_atom_g.

A branch of a stuck eliminator: the case of a constructor, binding a number of variables.
Record normal_branch_g (E : Set) : Set := mk_normal_branch
  {
The constructor the branch is the case of
    branch_constructor : string
    
The number of variables the branch binds: the member's non-uniform parameters, the arguments, and one recursive result per recursive argument
  ; branch_arity : nat
    
The branch's body, under those variables
  ; branch_body : E }.
Arguments mk_normal_branch {E}.
Arguments branch_constructor {E}.
Arguments branch_arity {E}.
Arguments branch_body {E}.
Scheme All for normal_branch_g.

A block of a stuck eliminator, one per member of the group, in the group's order.
Record normal_block_g (E : Set) : Set := mk_normal_block
  {
The number of variables the motive binds: the member's non-uniform parameters and the scrutinee
    block_arity : nat
    
The motive, under those variables
  ; block_motive : E
    
The branches, one per constructor of the member, in order
  ; block_branches : list (normal_branch_g E) }.
Arguments mk_normal_block {E}.
Arguments block_arity {E}.
Arguments block_motive {E}.
Arguments block_branches {E}.
Scheme All for normal_block_g.

Operations on the Records

A function on what the records hold acts on the records. A branch's body and a block's motive sit under binders, so the function on a branch or a block is told how many: the arity.
An atom with its neutral mapped.
Definition map_level_atom {E F : Set} (f : E -> F) (a : level_atom_g E) : level_atom_g F :=
  mk_level_atom (atom_offset a) (atom_sort a) (f (atom_level a)).

A branch with its body mapped, at its arity.
Definition map_normal_branch {E F : Set} (f : nat -> E -> F) (br : normal_branch_g E) : normal_branch_g F :=
  mk_normal_branch (branch_constructor br) (branch_arity br) (f (branch_arity br) (branch_body br)).

A block with its motive and its branches' bodies mapped, each at its arity.
Definition map_normal_block {E F : Set} (f : nat -> E -> F) (b : normal_block_g E) : normal_block_g F :=
  mk_normal_block (block_arity b) (f (block_arity b) (block_motive b))
    (List.map (map_normal_branch f) (block_branches b)).

P holds of a block's motive and of its branches' bodies, each at its arity.
Definition normal_block_forall {E : Set} (P : nat -> E -> Prop) (b : normal_block_g E) : Prop :=
  P (block_arity b) (block_motive b) /\ all_list (fun br => P (branch_arity br) (branch_body br)) (block_branches b).

The boolean normal_block_forall.
Definition normal_block_forallb {E : Set} (f : nat -> E -> bool) (b : normal_block_g E) : bool :=
  f (block_arity b) (block_motive b) && List.forallb (fun br => f (branch_arity br) (branch_body br)) (block_branches b).

Using the Generated Hypotheses

The induction principle of a type nesting through list and the records gives list_all of the motive at a list. These lemmas turn it into what a proof by that induction needs: equal maps, and all_list.
Lemma list_all_map_ext {A B : Set} (P : A -> Set) (f g : A -> B) : forall l,
    list_all A P l -> (forall x, P x -> f x = g x) -> List.map f l = List.map g l.
Proof. intros l Hl Hfg; induction Hl; cbn; f_equal; auto. Qed.

Lemma list_all_all_list {A : Set} (P : A -> Set) (Q : A -> Prop) : forall l,
    list_all A P l -> (forall x, P x -> Q x) -> all_list Q l.
Proof. intros l Hl HPQ; induction Hl; cbn; auto. Qed.

Lemma list_all_all_list_impl {A : Set} (P : A -> Set) (Q R : A -> Prop) : forall l,
    list_all A P l -> all_list Q l -> (forall x, P x -> Q x -> R x) -> all_list R l.
Proof. intros l Hl; induction Hl as [| x Hx l Hl IH]; cbn; [ auto | intros [Hq Hr] H; split; auto ]. Qed.

Lemma all_list_app {A : Set} (Q : A -> Prop) : forall l l',
    all_list Q l -> all_list Q l' -> all_list Q (l ++ l').
Proof. induction l as [| x l IH]; cbn; [ auto | intros l' [Hx Hl] Hl'; split; auto ]. Qed.

Lemma all_list_map {A B : Set} (f : A -> B) (Q : B -> Prop) : forall l,
    all_list Q (List.map f l) <-> all_list (fun x => Q (f x)) l.
Proof. induction l as [| x l IH]; cbn; [ reflexivity | rewrite IH; reflexivity ]. Qed.

Lemma list_all_Forall_map {A B : Set} (P : A -> Set) (Q : B -> Prop) (f : A -> B) : forall l,
    list_all A P l -> (forall x, P x -> Q (f x)) -> List.Forall Q (List.map f l).
Proof. intros l Hl HPQ; induction Hl; constructor; auto. Qed.

A goal List.map f l = List.map g l, or all_list R l, reduced to one goal per element x of l, from the generated hypothesis on l (and, for all_list, from an all_list hypothesis on l when there is one): Hx the motive at x, Hy that hypothesis at x. A record's _all hypothesis is taken apart, and with it the record.
Ltac nested_elements :=
  rewrite ?List.map_map;
  let x := fresh "x" in let Hx := fresh "Hx" in let Hy := fresh "Hy" in
  match goal with
  | Hl : list_all _ _ ?l |- List.map _ ?l = List.map _ ?l =>
      apply (list_all_map_ext _ _ _ l Hl); intros x Hx; try destruct Hx
  | Hl : list_all _ _ ?l, Hq : all_list _ ?l |- all_list _ ?l =>
      apply (list_all_all_list_impl _ _ _ l Hl Hq); intros x Hx Hy; try destruct Hx
  | Hl : list_all _ _ ?l |- all_list _ ?l =>
      apply (list_all_all_list _ _ l Hl); intros x Hx; try destruct Hx
  end.

Lemma list_all_forallb {A : Set} (P : A -> Set) (f : A -> bool) (Q : A -> Prop) : forall l,
    list_all A P l -> (forall x, P x -> f x = true <-> Q x) -> List.forallb f l = true <-> all_list Q l.
Proof.
  intros l Hl HfQ; induction Hl as [| x Hx l Hl IH]; cbn; [ split; auto |].
  rewrite Bool.andb_true_iff, (HfQ x Hx), IH; reflexivity.
Qed.

Inductive nf : Set :=
A large universe
| nf_typ : nat -> nf
A small universe at a canonical level max (c, k₁ + a₁, …), in the shape of nf_lvl below
| nf_univ : o2 -> list (level_atom_g ne) -> nf
The type Level@n
| nf_level : nat -> nf
A canonical level max (c, k₁ + a₁, …): the atoms are strictly sorted by their neutral and their sort (see Core.Syntactic.Levels.Levels) with no repetition, no atom is of a sort below the constant's tier (the constant absorbs it), and the constant c is 0 unless it exceeds every offset. nf_lvl_of builds the normal form of a canonical level lvl.
| nf_lvl : o2 -> list (level_atom_g ne) -> nf
⊤
| nf_True : nf
Its element
| nf_true : nf
⊥
| nf_False : nf
A Π of normal forms
| nf_pi : nf -> nf -> nf
A function, its domain and body normal
| nf_fn : nf -> nf -> nf
A member of a group of inductive types at its parameters
| nf_indty : qname -> nat -> list nf -> nf
A constructor at the parameters of its type and its arguments
| nf_con : qname -> nat -> string -> list nf -> nf
A neutral
| nf_neut : ne -> nf
A record type at its parameters
| nf_record : qname -> list nf -> nf
An element of the record type at p, η-long: the type's parameters, the field names and the fields
| nf_tuple : qname -> list nf -> list string -> list nf -> nf
with ne : Set :=
The ⊥-eliminator, always stuck
| ne_exfalso : nf -> ne -> ne
The eliminator of the group pq, at its declared member m, stuck on a neutral, at the group's uniform parameters; its blocks carry no annotation. (An eliminator at a view is stuck as the eliminator of the view's container's group.)
| ne_elim : qname -> list nf -> nat -> list (normal_block_g nf) -> ne -> ne
A neutral applied
| ne_app : ne -> nf -> ne
A variable
| ne_var : nat -> ne
An opaque definition or an axiom: it does not unfold.
| ne_glob : qname -> ne
A field of a neutral
| ne_proj : string -> ne -> ne.

The records at normal forms and neutrals.
Abbreviation level_atom := (level_atom_g ne).
Abbreviation normal_branch := (normal_branch_g nf).
Abbreviation normal_block := (normal_block_g nf).

The induction principle of normal forms and neutrals, generated: a list carries list_all of the motive, a record of the records above its own _all.
Scheme nf_nested_ind := Induction for nf Sort Prop
with ne_nested_ind := Induction for ne Sort Prop.
Combined Scheme nf_ne_ind from nf_nested_ind, ne_nested_ind.

M applied to args, outermost first.
Fixpoint apps_exp (M : exp) (args : list exp) : exp :=
  match args with
  | nil => M
  | N :: args' => apps_exp (a_app M N) args'
  end.

The term a normal form stands for (normal forms are a subset of terms).
Fixpoint nf_to_exp (M : nf) : exp :=
  match M with
  | nf_typ i => a_typ i
  | nf_univ c xs => a_univ (lvl_exp_of c (List.map (fun a => (atom_offset a, ne_to_exp (atom_level a))) xs))
  | nf_level n => a_level n
  | nf_lvl c xs => lvl_exp_of c (List.map (fun a => (atom_offset a, ne_to_exp (atom_level a))) xs)
  | nf_True => a_True
  | nf_true => a_true
  | nf_False => a_False
  | nf_pi A B => a_pi (nf_to_exp A) (nf_to_exp B)
  | nf_fn A M => a_fn (nf_to_exp A) (nf_to_exp M)
  | nf_indty p k Ms => apps_exp (a_ind p k) (List.map nf_to_exp Ms)
  | nf_con p k c Ms => apps_exp (a_con p k c) (List.map nf_to_exp Ms)
  | nf_neut M => ne_to_exp M
  | nf_record p Ms => apps_exp (a_record p) (List.map nf_to_exp Ms)
  | nf_tuple p Ms fs Ns => a_tuple (apps_exp (a_record p) (List.map nf_to_exp Ms)) (List.combine fs (List.map nf_to_exp Ns))
  end
with ne_to_exp (M : ne) : exp :=
  match M with
  | ne_exfalso A M => a_exfalso (nf_to_exp A) (ne_to_exp M)
  | ne_elim p Us m Bks M =>
      a_elim (Some p) (List.map nf_to_exp Us) m
        (List.map (fun b => eb_mk (block_arity b) None (nf_to_exp (block_motive b))
                              (List.map (fun br => (branch_constructor br, branch_arity br, nf_to_exp (branch_body br)))
                                 (block_branches b))) Bks)
        (ne_to_exp M)
  | ne_app M N => a_app (ne_to_exp M) (nf_to_exp N)
  | ne_var x => a_var x
  | ne_glob p => qname_term p
  | ne_proj f M => a_proj f (ne_to_exp M)
  end.

Coercion nf_to_exp : nf >-> exp.
Coercion ne_to_exp : ne >-> exp.

An atom of a canonical level as a term spells it: its offset, and the neutral level as a term.
Definition atom_exp (a : level_atom) : (nat * exp)%type := (atom_offset a, ne_to_exp (atom_level a)).

A branch of a stuck eliminator as a term's branch.
Definition branch_exp (br : normal_branch) : (string * nat * exp)%type :=
  (branch_constructor br, branch_arity br, nf_to_exp (branch_body br)).

A block of a stuck eliminator as a term's block: it carries no annotation.
Definition block_exp (b : normal_block) : eblock :=
  eb_mk (block_arity b) None (nf_to_exp (block_motive b)) (List.map branch_exp (block_branches b)).

The clauses of nf_to_exp at the levels and at a stuck eliminator, through the definitions above.
Lemma nf_to_exp_univ : forall c xs, nf_to_exp (nf_univ c xs) = a_univ (lvl_exp_of c (List.map atom_exp xs)).
Proof. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma nf_to_exp_lvl : forall c xs, nf_to_exp (nf_lvl c xs) = lvl_exp_of c (List.map atom_exp xs).
Proof. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma ne_to_exp_elim : forall p Us m Bks M,
    ne_to_exp (ne_elim p Us m Bks M) = a_elim (Some p) (List.map nf_to_exp Us) m (List.map block_exp Bks) (ne_to_exp M).
Proof. reflexivity. Qed.

Canonical Levels

A canonical level is its constant and its atoms. The operations on canonical levels, and their order, are Core.Syntactic.Levels.Levels; the type is here because the universe normal forms below are indexed by it.
Definition lvl : Set := (o2 * list level_atom)%type.

Definition nf_lvl_of (l : lvl) : nf := nf_lvl (fst l) (snd l).

Definition nf_univ_of (l : lvl) : nf := nf_univ (fst l) (snd l).

Lemma nf_lvl_of_inj : forall l l', nf_lvl_of l = nf_lvl_of l' -> l = l'.
Proof.
  intros [c xs] [d ys] H; unfold nf_lvl_of in H; cbn in H.
  inversion H; reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma nf_univ_of_cong : forall l l', nf_lvl_of l = nf_lvl_of l' -> nf_univ_of l = nf_univ_of l'.
Proof. intros ? ? H; apply nf_lvl_of_inj in H as ->; reflexivity. Qed.

Universe Normal Forms

The universe a type is inferred at, as the algorithmic layer sees it: a small universe at a canonical level, or a large one. It is not the semantic index universe_index: a small universe's semantic index is the realiser of its level, an ordinal below ω², while the checker compares the canonical levels themselves (see Core.Syntactic.Levels.Levels: unf_le, unf_max).
Inductive unf : Set :=
A small universe at a canonical level
| uns : lvl -> unf
The large universe Typeω²+n
| unl : nat -> unf.

Coercion unl : nat >-> unf.

The universe normal form itself, and the term it embeds to.
Definition univ_nf (u : unf) : nf :=
  match u with uns L => nf_univ_of L | unl n => nf_typ n end.

Definition unf_tm (u : unf) : exp :=
  match u with
  | uns L => a_univ (lvl_exp_of (fst L) (List.map atom_exp (snd L)))
  | unl n => a_typ n
  end.

Lemma nf_to_exp_univ_nf : forall u, nf_to_exp (univ_nf u) = unf_tm u.
Proof. intros [[] |]; reflexivity. Qed.

That a normal form is a universe. This is the side condition of every algorithmic rule that asks for a type. It is a relation and not an equation f W = Some u of a deciding function f: the left-hand side of that equation is a match stuck on W, and progressive_inversion does not terminate on such a hypothesis — it inverts it to an equation of the same shape, for ever.
Variant is_univ_nf : nf -> unf -> Prop :=
| is_univ_nf_typ : forall i, is_univ_nf (nf_typ i) (unl i)
| is_univ_nf_univ : forall c xs, is_univ_nf (nf_univ c xs) (uns (c, xs)).

Lemma is_univ_nf_univ_nf : forall u, is_univ_nf (univ_nf u) u.
Proof. intros [[] |]; constructor. Qed.

Lemma is_univ_nf_eq : forall W u, is_univ_nf W u -> W = univ_nf u.
Proof. intros ? ? H; destruct H; reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma is_univ_nf_functional : forall W u v, is_univ_nf W u -> is_univ_nf W v -> u = v.
Proof. intros ? ? ? H H'; destruct H; inversion H'; reflexivity. Qed.

A normal form with no global at the head of a neutral.
Fixpoint nf_clean (W : nf) : Prop :=
  match W with
  | nf_typ _ | nf_level _ | nf_True | nf_true | nf_False => True
  | nf_univ _ xs | nf_lvl _ xs => all_list (fun a => ne_clean (atom_level a)) xs
  | nf_pi A B | nf_fn A B => nf_clean A /\ nf_clean B
  | nf_indty _ _ Ms | nf_con _ _ _ Ms => all_list nf_clean Ms
  | nf_neut M => ne_clean M
  | nf_record _ Ms => all_list nf_clean Ms
  | nf_tuple _ Ms _ Ns => all_list nf_clean Ms /\ all_list nf_clean Ns
  end
with ne_clean (M : ne) : Prop :=
  match M with
  | ne_exfalso A M => nf_clean A /\ ne_clean M
  | ne_elim _ Us _ Bks M =>
      all_list nf_clean Us /\
      all_list (fun b => nf_clean (block_motive b) /\ all_list (fun br => nf_clean (branch_body br)) (block_branches b)) Bks /\
      ne_clean M
  | ne_app M N => ne_clean M /\ nf_clean N
  | ne_var _ => True
  | ne_glob _ => False
  | ne_proj _ M => ne_clean M
  end.

Decidable equality of the records of normal forms, given that of what they hold.
Section RecordDec.
  Context {E : Set} (de : forall x y : E, {x = y} + {x <> y}).

  Definition level_atom_eq_dec_g (a a' : level_atom_g E) : {a = a'} + {a <> a'}.
  Proof.
    destruct a as [k s u], a' as [k' s' u'].
    destruct (PeanoNat.Nat.eq_dec k k') as [<- |]; [| right; congruence ].
    destruct (PeanoNat.Nat.eq_dec s s') as [<- |]; [| right; congruence ].
    destruct (de u u') as [<- |]; [ left; reflexivity | right; congruence ].
  Defined.

  Definition normal_branch_eq_dec_g (b b' : normal_branch_g E) : {b = b'} + {b <> b'}.
  Proof.
    destruct b as [c n B], b' as [c' n' B'].
    destruct (String.string_dec c c') as [<- |]; [| right; congruence ].
    destruct (PeanoNat.Nat.eq_dec n n') as [<- |]; [| right; congruence ].
    destruct (de B B') as [<- |]; [ left; reflexivity | right; congruence ].
  Defined.

  Definition normal_block_eq_dec_g (b b' : normal_block_g E) : {b = b'} + {b <> b'}.
  Proof.
    destruct b as [nm A Bs], b' as [nm' A' Bs'].
    destruct (PeanoNat.Nat.eq_dec nm nm') as [<- |]; [| right; congruence ].
    destruct (de A A') as [<- |]; [| right; congruence ].
    destruct (List.list_eq_dec normal_branch_eq_dec_g Bs Bs') as [<- |]; [ left; reflexivity | right; congruence ].
  Defined.
End RecordDec.

Equality of normal forms and neutrals is decidable.
Fixpoint nf_eq_dec (M M' : nf) {struct M} : {M = M'} + {M <> M'}
with ne_eq_dec (M M' : ne) {struct M} : {M = M'} + {M <> M'}.
Proof.
Names are compared by string_dec, before decide equality could take a string apart character by character.
  all: decide equality;
    first [ apply PeanoNat.Nat.eq_dec | apply String.string_dec | apply qname_eq_dec | apply o2_eq_dec
          | apply (List.list_eq_dec String.string_dec) | apply (List.list_eq_dec nf_eq_dec)
          | apply (List.list_eq_dec (level_atom_eq_dec_g ne_eq_dec))
